discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 041740
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
140 PM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Primarily dry conditions are expected through this work week.

- After starting out with slightly below normal high temps,
  highs slightly above normal take over for the end of the work
  week.

- Cold Tuesday morning with lows dipping down to the 30s for
  some areas north of US-6.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 128 PM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

Behind this morning's cold front, a reinforcing shot of cool air 
moves in. That allows today's highs in the 70s, generally south of 
US-6, to drop back into the 60s everywhere for Monday. When we get 
the better frost scenarios, it's usually on the heels of a 
temperature upswing like happens as we head into midweek this week. 
I usually like to see at least 3 hours of 36 to 38F temperatures 
with light to calm winds and minimal cloud cover to get a good setup 
for frost. However, it appears that warm advection moves in Monday 
night and this sets up the chance for mid to upper cloudiness at 
least in areas west of IN-15 (if you continued it into MI) and north 
of US-6. NAM Bufkit soundings appear to indicate some decoupling, 
but those mid to upper 30s for a few hours may still be hard to come 
by. The NASA SPoRT LIS actually shows less than 30 percent 0-100 cm 
soil moisture percentile up in St Joseph to Hillsdale and LaGrange 
to Fulton OH counties, but we've added rain to that area in the last 
week or so and this may make radiational cooling not entirely as 
efficient as may be needed. This combination of factors would still 
point to areas north of the Toll road having the best chance for 
frost, but think more patchy frost as opposed to widespread and this 
may be relegated to outlying areas. High temperatures stay in the 
upper 60s to upper 70s the rest of the forecast period.

Aside from that, dry weather continues. A dry cold front washes out 
and stalls nearby Wednesday into Thursday time period before pushing 
back northeastward Friday into Saturday. The ECMWF has rain in the 
vicinity of our area Thursday night, but its moisture column 
looks rather dry overhead. The next chance for rain could come 
as early as Saturday night, but may wait until Sunday/Sunday 
night. This is as a deep cutoff low makes its way northward from
the south/southwest bringing moisture with it. It has times of 
large scale ascent that may be able to squeeze moisture out, but
little instability.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z MONDAY/...
Issued at 1203 PM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

VFR through the period. A cold front will move through during 
the early to mid afternoon hours today with a wind shift to the 
northwest (near 10 kts). No precip, or even much of the way of 
cloud cover, expected with the fropa given the overall dearth 
of column moisture. High pressure will build into tonight with 
light winds and mainly clear skies.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 041928

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0228 PM CDT Sun Oct 04 2026

   Valid 042000Z - 051200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE FLORIDA PANHANDLE/FAR SOUTHERN ALABAMA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few rotating thunderstorms are possible today across parts of the
   Florida Panhandle/far southern Alabama.

   ...20z Update...
   No changes were made to the current D1 Convective Outlook. See
   previous discussion below for more information.

   ..Thornton.. 10/04/2026

   .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1125 AM CDT Sun Oct 04 2026/

   ...Florida Panhandle/Far Southern Alabama...
   A nearly stationary surface front will reside across the Southeast
   today, with a very moist airmass (total PWAT values of 2+ inches)
   persisting along and to its south. Scattered showers/thunderstorms
   will continue to develop south of the front this afternoon,
   including across the northern Gulf. It is still possible that a weak
   offshore surface low may form later today, with modest enhancement
   to the low-level flow and effective SRH near a weak boundary draped
   along or just offshore the FL Panhandle and far southern AL. Should
   this occur, convection may have the potential to exhibit transient
   low-level circulations mainly near the coast, with related
   waterspout/brief tornado potential. However, the severe threat will
   likely be constrained by poor lapse rates/weak instability, with
   some guidance (namely recent RAP runs) suggesting that the modest
   increase in low-level flow may not occur.

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0100Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 041715

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1215 PM CDT Sun Oct 04 2026

   Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low over the eastern Great Lakes and St Lawrence Valley is
   forecast to intensify as it moves eastward into the Northeast States
   and offshore Monday. In the wake of the upper low, northwest flow is
   forecast across much of the central and eastern CONUS. A weak
   shortwave trough will traverse the northern Great Basin on the
   periphery of ridging over the Southwest.

   At the surface, a cold front will continue to sag southward across
   the Gulf Coast with high pressure intensifying behind it over the
   Midwest. Stable conditions are forecast for much of the central and
   eastern States. Substantial low-level moisture and instability will
   be confined to the Gulf Coast and much of FL near the front.
   Scattered thunderstorms are possible, though poor lapse rates and
   little overlap with favorable deep-layer shear suggest severe
   potential is unlikely.

   Occasional lightning is possible over the northern Great Basin and
   central Rockies ahead of the aforementioned shortwave trough.
   Instability will be weak, but steep mid-level lapse rates could
   promote some gusty surface winds with high-based
   showers/thunderstorms.

   ..Lyons.. 10/04/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0600Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 041927

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0227 PM CDT Sun Oct 04 2026

   Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A strong upper low, initially over the East Coast, will continue to
   move offshore as a second broader trough and strong jet move into
   the northern US from southern Canada. The increasingly strong
   northwesterly flow aloft and a surface cold front will reinforce a
   cooler and stable high pressure air mass over much of the central
   and eastern CONUS. Northerly offshore surface winds extending to the
   Gulf and Atlantic Coasts will limit available moisture for much of
   the US.

   Thunderstorm chances will be confined to the immediate Gulf Coast
   and FL where weak shear and poor lapse rates should preclude any
   organized severe risk. Additional scattered showers and
   thunderstorms may affect the eastern Great Basin and Four Corners
   region as a weak midlevel wave moves over the area steepening
   low/mid-level lapse rates. Storm coverage should remain low and a
   severe risk is unlikely given weak instability and deep-layer shear.

   ..Lyons.. 10/04/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
